questions.q: Define outsourcing in one sentence using the terms "non-core activity," "external agency," and "core competency."
questions.a: Outsourcing is the delegation of non-core activities to an external agency so the firm can concentrate on its core competency. A wrong answer that says "outsourcing means sending jobs to another country" reveals the offshoring misconception; a response missing "core competency" shows the student views outsourcing as mere cost-cutting rather than strategic focus.

questions.q: A textile manufacturer in Tirupur outsources its fabric dyeing to a specialised effluent-treatment-compliant dyeing unit. Explain why this is outsourcing and not merely subcontracting, using the concept of "strategic control over the process."
questions.a: In outsourcing, the client retains strategic control over *what* is done and *quality standards* while the vendor decides *how* to execute; in subcontracting, the principal often dictates the method. The textile firm sets colour fastness and environmental standards (strategic control) but lets the dyeing unit choose chemicals and machinery (operational control). A wrong answer equating the two indicates the student cannot distinguish governance models.

questions.q: A Mumbai-based fintech startup is deciding whether to outsource its customer-onboarding KYC verification. List the three decision bases (cost, expertise, focus) and give one specific data point the startup should collect for *each* base to make an evidence-based decision.
questions.a: Cost: compare in-house KYC cost per customer (salary + software + office space) vs. vendor quote per verification. Expertise: verify vendor’s RBI-compliance track record and error-rate percentage. Focus: estimate management hours currently spent on KYC audits that could shift to product development. Missing any base or giving generic "saves money" without a measurable metric shows inability to apply the framework.

questions.q: Compare the scope of outsourcing in a traditional brick-and-mortar retail chain versus a pure-play e-commerce platform. Identify two activities each would likely outsource and two they would keep in-house, justifying with "core vs. non-core" logic.
questions.a: Retail chain: outsource (1) store cleaning/security (non-core, standardised), (2) payroll processing (non-core, compliance-heavy); keep in-house (1) merchandise buying (core — defines brand), (2) store layout design (core — customer experience). E-commerce: outsource (1) last-mile delivery (non-core, scale-intensive), (2) payment gateway management (non-core, specialised tech); keep in-house (1) recommendation algorithm (core — differentiation), (2) seller onboarding policy (core — platform trust). Wrong classifications reveal fuzzy understanding of "core competency" in different business models.

questions.q: Critique the statement: "Outsourcing always reduces operational risk because the vendor bears the responsibility." Use the concepts of "vendor lock-in," "data confidentiality," and "service-level agreements" in your evaluation.
questions.a: The statement is false. Outsourcing *transfers* execution risk but *creates* new risks: vendor lock-in (switching costs make the firm dependent), data confidentiality breaches (vendor accesses sensitive customer/financial data), and SLA disputes (downtime penalties may not cover reputational loss). A student agreeing without caveats shows inability to evaluate risk trade-offs — a senior-secondary analytical gap.

questions.q: Design a 3-column "Outsourcing Decision Matrix" for a mid-sized Indian auto-component manufacturer. Columns: Activity, Core/Non-Core (with 1-line reason), Outsource? (Yes/No with primary basis: Cost/Expertise/Focus). Include at least 6 activities spanning manufacturing, R&D, and support functions.
questions.a: Example rows: (1) CNC machining of engine blocks — Core (proprietary tolerances) — No; (2) Heat treatment — Non-core (standardised process) — Yes, Cost; (3) Material science research — Core (future IP) — No; (4) Prototype 3D printing — Non-core (intermittent need) — Yes, Expertise; (5) Canteen services — Non-core (zero strategic value) — Yes, Cost; (6) GST return filing — Non-core (compliance) — Yes, Expertise. A matrix missing "reason" column or using only "Cost" basis shows superficial application.
